question: A bus can run 20% faster than a bike. Both start from the same place at the same time and reach the same destination 60 km away at the same time. On the way, however, the bus stops at the stations for 10 minutes. The speed of the bike is:
solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 60 km

Bus stops for 10 minutes

Bus is 20% faster than bike

**Concept/Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the bike be 's' km/h

Then, the speed of the bus = 120% of 's' = 1.2s km/h

Stoppage time of bus = 10 minutes = 1/6 hrs.

Time taken by bike = 60/s hrs

Time taken by bus = 60/1.2s hrs

∵ Both bike & bus reach their destination at the same time, the time taken by the bike = the time taken by the bus(including stoppage time) 

⇒ 60/s = 60/1.2s + (1/6)

⇒ 60/s = 60/1.2s + (1/6)

⇒ 60/s - 60/1.2s = 1/6

⇒ 60[1/s - 1/1.2s] = 1/6

⇒ 60(0.2/1.2s) =1/6

⇒ 60(1/6s) = 1/6 ⇒ 60 = s

**Therefore, the speed of the bike is 60 km/h.**
